reason: The cited evidence shows CeO2-based materials can enhance activity and durability via oxygen release and redox properties (E1) and that stable Ce–O–M bonds in high-entropy oxides improve thermal/hydrothermal stability (E2), but neither study involves a multi-element alloy catalyst or the specific CeO2 nanolayer deposition on such an alloy, leaving key premises about the alloy system and intervention unsupported.
premises: CeO2 provides oxygen storage/release and redox activity that can enhance catalytic performance and durability
A CeO2 nanolayer can stabilize active sites and reduce sintering/leaching under hydrothermal and thermal aging
Stable interfacial bonds (e.g., Ce–O–M) with catalyst elements are formed and contribute to stability
The intervention is effective for multi-element alloy catalysts under low-temperature, transient exhaust conditions with H2O and NO
